en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Confession (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Sahadhammika-vagga 71.
The Training Rule on Fellow Practitioners.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Channa was practicing improper conduct.
The bhikkhus said to him:
"Friend Channa, do not do such a thing."
"This is not allowable.
He says this:
"Friends, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another monk who is learned and an expert in the Vinaya."
Those bhikkhus who were of few desires... [and so on]... they complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can the Venerable Channa, when being spoken to by the bhikkhus in accordance with the Dhamma, say:
‘Friends, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is learned and an expert in the Vinaya’?”... [and so on]...
“Is it true, Channa, that when you were being addressed by the bhikkhus in accordance with the Dhamma, you spoke thus:
‘Friends, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another bhikkhu who is competent and a master of the Vinaya’?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“… How can you, foolish man, when being spoken to by the monks in accordance with the Dhamma, say:
‘Friends, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another monk who is competent and an expert in the Vinaya’?”
“Monk, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:
‘Whatever monk, when being spoken to by other monks in accordance with the Dhamma, should say: “Friends, I will not [accept] this until...”’”
‘I will train in this training rule until I have questioned another monk who is experienced and a bearer of the Vinaya,’ there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Monks, a monk who is training must understand, question, and inquire. This is the proper conduct in this matter.
As for “whoever”:
Whoever is such as this … [and so on] … “a bhikkhu” … [and so on] … this is the meaning intended here by the term “bhikkhu.”
"By bhikkhus" means by other bhikkhus.
"In accordance with the Dhamma" (sahadhammikaṃ) means:
That training rule which has been laid down by the Blessed One is called "in accordance with the Dhamma.

When being addressed by means of that, he says: "Friends, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another monk who is learned, expert, and wise. [He addresses] one who is wise, expert, and intelligent.
If one says, "I shall question the learned one who is a preacher of the Dhamma," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one addresses someone who is fully ordained (upasampanna) with the perception that they are fully ordained, saying this, there is an offense of expiation.
If one addresses someone who is fully ordained while being in doubt as to whether they are fully ordained, saying this, there is an offense of expiation.
If one who is fully ordained, perceiving another as not fully ordained, speaks thus, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
When being addressed with what is not prescribed:

"This is not for the sake of effacement, nor for the sake of the ascetic qualities, nor for the sake of inspiring confidence, nor for the sake of reduction, nor for the sake of the arousal of energy..."

If he says, "It leads [to such-and-such]," and then says, "Friends, I will not train in this training rule until I have questioned another monk who is experienced, an expert in the Vinaya, wise, intelligent, learned,
and a preacher of the Dhamma," he commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
When being addressed by one who is not fully ordained— whether regarding what has been prescribed or what has not been prescribed—
if he says, "This does not lead to effacement, nor to the purpose of ascetic purification, nor to inspiring confidence, nor to reduction [of defilements],
nor to the arousal of energy," and says, "Friend, I will not train in this training rule until..."
If he says, “I do not question another monk who is proficient, an expert in the Vinaya, wise, intelligent, learned,
and a preacher of the Dhamma,” there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If [the person addressed] is not one who has received full ordination, but he perceives him as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one is doubtful that the person is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If the person is not fully ordained and one perceives them as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
"By a female trainee" (sikkhamānāya) means...
"By one desiring to train.
"Should be known" means it should be understood.
"Paripucchitabbaṃ" means:
"Venerable sir, what is this? Or what is the meaning of this? "Paripaṇhitabbaṃ" means:
[to be investigated].
It should be reflected upon and weighed.
This is the proper conduct therein;
this is the accordance with the Dhamma therein.
There is no offense if he says, "I shall know; I shall train," or if he is insane.
"For one who is a first-time offender.
The first training rule concerning those who live according to the Dhamma is finished.
